name: Diego Zaragoza-Kettani
location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone, sleeps at his aunt's flat, near Michigan Ave and Walton
description:
Tarquin is all elbows and velocity — a tall, wiry teenager with dark brown skin, a close-cut fade, and his father's Ghanaian cheekbones softened by his mother's Bolivian jaw. He has a single cosmetic mod he saved for three months to afford: a cat tail in iridescent black that he swishes when he's thinking and tucks carefully into his waistband when his aunt is home. His fingers are permanently stained with aerosolized pigment in colors that shift weekly. He carries a battered recording rig everywhere — a shoulder-mounted camera array he built from three broken units cannibalized at the Brightmoor Reclamation salvage markets.

Tarquin is the kind of talented that hasn't yet been shaped by knowing it, which makes his work both raw and startling — he films while he sprays, combines the visual and the documentary without quite understanding that's an unusual thing to do, and the result is a growing archive of HPAZ street art that is also an accidental ethnography of a community holding itself together. He is cocky in the way of someone who knows they're good but hasn't been tested, and genuinely kind in the way of someone raised by people who expected it. He is currently engaged in a low-grade obsessive competition with another writer whose tag, 'Çukur,' keeps appearing over or beside his own work — he hasn't decided yet if it's a rivalry or a conversation.

core_fears: The HPAZ being absorbed or dissolved — losing the only place he's felt like he belongs
Becoming boring, becoming safe, becoming someone who used to make things
core_desires: To be taken seriously without having to get older to deserve it
To find Çukur and figure out if they're an enemy or the most interesting person he's ever met
coping_mechanisms: Makes something — if he's upset, he goes and sprays; the act of making is regulation
Turns everything into content — documentary distance from things that scare him
blind_spots: Films other people's vulnerability without always asking permission, because to him visibility is inherently positive
Doesn't think about the legal and physical risks of his locations clearly enough
psychology.secret: Two months ago, while filming in the drainage access corridors beneath the HPAZ, he recorded what he's pretty sure was a Ringo corporate extraction team moving something large and organic through a route that isn't on any map. He hasn't uploaded it. He's watched the raw footage seventeen times. He doesn't know what he's waiting for.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast slang, HPAZ youth vernacular, Twi words inherited from his father, Spanish phrases from his mother; switches registers abruptly when talking to adults he respects
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid-fire when excited; goes unusually quiet and specific when he's being serious about the work
verbal_tics: 'It's documented' (meaning he filmed it and it's therefore real and important)
example_lines: 'Çukur came back over my cloud piece on the Kessler junction wall, but — and this is the thing — they left a gap right where I had the negative space. They knew what I was doing. That's not beef, that's a response.'
'It's documented. Whatever Ringo is moving through those drains, it's documented. I just have to decide what that means.'

story_hooks: The Ringo footage — Tarquin eventually needs to tell someone, and whoever he tells gets pulled into whatever that was
Çukur reaches out, not in person but through a piece — a wall that is clearly a message to TQ specifically, with coordinates embedded in the design
narrative_function: Local color, youth perspective, mobile observer — he goes places adults can't or won't and records what's there; his footage is a resource; he can draw characters into the HPAZ community or into whatever he's currently chasing.
augmentations: Iridescent black cat tail (geneware, cosmetic); no other mods
daily_life: School until midday (technically — attendance is irregular), works afternoons and nights on walls and filming, uploads edited cuts to underground data-shares under the handle 'TQ/HPAZ', back before dawn when possible.
affiliation: No formal collective; loosely orbiting the Highland Park Autonomous Zone youth arts program Inkwell

decision_rules: If you can see it, you should film it — visibility is dignity
Don't mess with other writers' pieces without leaving your tag; anonymous destruction is cowardice
escalation_ladder: Retreating behind the camera — becomes observer rather than participant
Genuine anger, which is rare and startling given his usual energy
Going completely silent and disappearing to make something

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Confident front, quick to joke, slow to trust — assesses whether they see the HPAZ as a place or a problem first
interpersonal_modes.friends: Fiercely loyal, would do genuinely stupid things for people he loves, expresses affection through showing up

stress_responses.medium: Focuses obsessively on a specific piece or project to the exclusion of everything else
stress_responses.high: Goes out to spray alone at 3am in locations that are more dangerous than he's admitting to himself

contradictions: Insists he's not afraid of anything while carefully avoiding re-watching the last thirty seconds of the Ringo footage
habits: Names every piece he completes — not publicly, just in his own log
Talks to his cat tail when he thinks no one can hear him
Leaves a small tag — a single dot in the specific shade he calls 'signal orange' — on every location he films, a private archive marker
breaking_points: Watching the HPAZ be dismantled or occupied by corporate forces without being able to do anything
Someone being hurt because of something he filmed

cyberware_inventory.name: Salvage-built shoulder-mount camera array (three-unit composite, TQ's own construction)

timeline.event: 2183: Born in Highland Park Autonomous Zone to a Ghanaian father and Bolivian mother
2191: Father left for work in the Calumet Rise industrial district; irregular contact since
2196: First wall piece on the HPAZ eastern border, age 13
2199: Started combining filming with spraying; began uploading to underground data-shares
2200: Recorded the Ringo footage in the drainage corridor

physical_description.heritage: Hispanic/Latin American (68.4%) with significant East Asian (21.9%) and North African (9.7%) ancestry. The genetic blend creates a striking fusion: warm medium-brown skin with subtle golden undertones from the Latin American base, enhanced by the East Asian cheekbone structure and the North African depth to his complexion. His features reflect this diaspora mix — angular and defined from multiple ancestry lines converging.
physical_description.build: Wiry and angular — all lean muscle and restless energy, the build of someone who climbs and runs and rarely sits still. Long limbs, sharp shoulders, minimal body fat.
physical_description.hair_style: Close-cut fade with precise geometric lines, maintained weekly; no styling products, let it air-dry into clean definition
physical_description.skin_tone: Medium-warm brown with golden undertones; sun-darkened from outdoor work, showing the blended warmth of Latin American and East Asian ancestry with North African depth. Not evenly tanned — darker on exposed areas from consistent outdoor climbing and spray-painting work.
physical_description.complexion: Clear skin with a sparse scatter of acne across his upper back and shoulders from summer heat and outdoor sweating. Strong cheekbones reflecting East Asian-Latin American blend, balanced by a warm jawline. No facial hair — too young, or keeps it shaved. Permanent pigment staining on his fingertips and cuticles in shifting colors: current palette shows traces of cadmium yellow, metallic silver, and hot pink beneath the embedded aerosol dust.
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Iridescent black cat tail (living geneware implant, 40cm long) emerging from base of spine, covered in fine black fur with an opalescent sheen that shifts blue-green-purple in certain light; he keeps it tucked into his waistband or cargo pockets when indoors with his aunt, but wears it loose when working. Recording rig (shoulder-mounted camera array, three separate units cannibalized and rewired) is an external accessory carried constantly — weathered, held together with epoxy and electrical tape, covered in stickers and worn paint.
distinguishing_marks: Iridescent black cat tail (living geneware implant, 40cm long) emerging from base of spine, covered in fine black fur with an opalescent sheen that shifts blue-green-purple in certain light; moves independently with mood and cognition
Small burn scar on his left forearm (5cm, linear) from a salvage yard accident two years ago with a hot flux capacitor; faded but visible
Faint scarring on both knuckles from spray-can pressure cuts and small lacerations from concrete climbing
physical_description.posture_movement: Perpetually in motion — fidgeting, shifting weight, bouncing on the balls of his feet. When focused on work (spraying, filming, editing), he goes still with an almost meditative intensity. Climbs and moves through three-dimensional space with practiced ease; comfortable on fire escapes, ledges, scaffolding. His tail moves in counterpoint to his body language: swishing when excited or thinking, tucking when anxious. Walks with a slight forward lean, as if always heading somewhere interesting.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 working-class aesthetics with art-scene individualism. Favors oversized hoodies (often paint-stained, deliberately or accidentally), slim cargo pants with deep pockets for supplies, reinforced tactical boots scuffed and weathered from climbing. Wears a canvas satchel across his chest (cannibalized from a courier bag, patched with fabric tape) that holds spray cans, tools, and backup recording media. His aunt bought him a Brightmoor reclamation puffer vest last winter; he wears it unzipped over hoodies. No expensive brands; everything is either salvaged, thrifted, or bought secondhand at the Highland Park market stalls. His color palette mirrors his spray-paint choices — one week heavy on grays and blacks, the next unexpected pops of neon through a thrifted windbreaker. All his clothes show evidence of his work: paint spatters, singe marks, dust from climbing.
